era.policy: ships iff era rank <= CURRENT_ERA rank, or the item is in the live client export, or the player named it; everything else is quarantined to pipeline/quarantine.json and never reaches the payload. Era-less is unconfirmed, not presumed classic: the few era-less items that do ship are the ones Tier 0 vouches for, and they carry eraUnknown:true. Everything shipped is available (av:true) — there is no client-side era gate.

slots.anyPolicy: items with an:1 may be placed in either "Any Slot" position; no ANY shard is emitted (it would duplicate every worn item)

sourceStanding.principle: Existence and stat provenance are two facts, not one. The live inventory export proves an item is in the game and carries no stat values at all; the validation captures prove particular numbers. Every shipped record states both, and states them separately.

flags.summary: The wiki carries two authoring conventions and the flag vocabulary partitions between them. The client disagrees with the catalog on both Tier 0 items sampled.
findings: NO_DROP and NO_TRADE never co-occur: 0 of 7,813 pages carrying a flag line have both.
NO_DROP appears on 3355 legacy-style pages and 0 modern-style pages.
MAGIC appears on 5398 legacy-style pages and 0 modern-style pages.
PLACEABLE appears on 20 modern-style pages and 1 legacy-style pages, so it is recorded only by the newer convention.

The client renders "No Trade" for Whitened Treant Fists, whose legacy-style page says NO DROP. Combined with the zero co-occurrence and the clean partition by page style, NO_DROP is most likely the same restriction the client calls No Trade, under the older spelling. This is NOT asserted in the data: both flags ship exactly as the wiki spells them.
MAGIC is absent from every modern-style page and from both client screenshots, so it may be a classic-EverQuest concept EQL no longer surfaces. Unresolved.
flags.openQuestion: Are NO_DROP and NO_TRADE one restriction or two? Resolving it needs more client samples, ideally an item whose page uses the modern convention.

weaponSkill.summary: Spelling is normalized to the client vocabulary; no weapon has been moved between skills. The wiki itself appears wrong for fist-type Monk weapons.
evidence: Our parse is faithful: all four independent scrapes report 1H Blunt for this item, and the wiki page category is 1H Blunt too.

The wiki is internally inconsistent within one item family: Bronze, Rusty and Steel Knuckles are Hand to Hand, while Brass Knuckles, Knuckle Dusters and every Velium Knuckledusters variant are 1H Blunt.
Only 11 items in the whole catalog carry Hand to Hand, and all are low damage (3-12); the high-end Monk fist gear is all skilled 1H Blunt.
Scope of possible error: 130 MNK-usable weapons carry a skill; 38 are MNK-only (1H Blunt 17, 2H Blunt 13, Hand to Hand 7, Throwing 1).
weaponSkill.suspectRule: weapon usable by MNK (explicit class list, not ALL/ALL_EXCEPT) whose name matches /fist|knuckle|claw|cestus|ulak|fistwrap/i and whose wiki skill is not "Hand to Hand"

dmgBonus.note: The client shows a Dmg Bon line (13 on Whitened Treant Fists, 50 on Earthshaker). No source carries it per item; jmoyers has it on 1 item only. It is probably derived from character level and weapon type. `wp.bonus` is emitted only where a source actually printed it.

itemIds.note: Only 299 of 3663 items have a numeric id; they come from a live client export, not from any wiki source.

unstattedKnownItems.policy: exists in the game, no source carries stats; never scored, ranked or auto-filled. Each record carries an `evidence` string naming what proves it exists.

existenceOnly.rule: ships iff EQL Source names it — measured dropping in data/sightings.v1.json, or listed in the name-to-game-ID table data/items.v1.json — and no wiki source carries a record for it
existenceOnly.policy: no slot, no class, no era, no stats. It cannot be equipped, ranked, scored or auto-filled, because nothing about it has been measured except that the game produced it. The name of a piece of armour makes its slot obvious; obvious is not observed.

purge.rule: ships iff pre-Kunark era, or Tier M evidence places it in the game
